Hey all. I'm working on a Lean 4 formalization (Mathlib v4.28.0) and I'm stuck on one specific convergence lemma. I'm hoping there may already be a theorem in Mathlib or PNTAnd that I've missed.

I need a result of the form:

∃ L : ℂ, Tendsto
(fun N => ∑ n ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N,
↑(ArithmeticFunction.moebius n) * (↑n : ℂ) ^ (-(1 + 2 * ↑t * Complex.I)))
Filter.atTop (nhds L)

for real t ≠ 0.

Informally: convergence of ∑ μ(n) n^{-(1+2it)} at a nonzero boundary point on Re(s)=1. I already have ζ(1+2it) ≠ 0 proved in my formalization, so the non-vanishing hypothesis is available.

What I've found so far:

  • mu_pnt_alt in PNTAnd handles the special case at s = 1
  • ArithmeticFunction.LSeriesSummable_moebius_iff seems to only give absolute convergence for Re(s) > 1
  • I found LSeriesHasSum / LSeriesSummable, but I can't tell whether they cover boundary-point convergence
  • A direct Abel summation attempt doesn't seem to close, since the variation of n^(-2it) grows like log N

So the question is:

  1. Does a formalized theorem already exist in Mathlib or PNTAnd that gives convergence of the Möbius Dirichlet series at s = 1+2it when t ≠ 0?
  2. More generally, is there already a formalized Tauberian/Newman/Ingham-style result that upgrades analyticity / nonvanishing of 1/ζ(s) at a boundary point on Re(s)=1 into convergence of the Dirichlet series there?

If not, is there an existing Wiener/Tauberian path in PNTAnd that is intended to be extended in exactly this direction?

Any pointers would be appreciated. Thanks.
Hey, welcome! Could you please make your question into a #mwe ?

Absolutely. Thanks (& my apologies, I'm still learning the ropes)! Here's an #mwe that compiles clean on Mathlib v4.28.0 (only diagnostic is the sorry):

import Mathlib.NumberTheory.ArithmeticFunction.Moebius
import Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Dirichlet
import Mathlib.Analysis.SpecialFunctions.Complex.CircleAddChar

open Complex Finset Filter ArithmeticFunction

/-- Convergence of the Möbius Dirichlet series ∑ μ(n) n^{-(1+2it)} for t ≠ 0.
Classical: follows from ζ(1+2it) ≠ 0 via Newman's Tauberian theorem. -/
theorem moebius_dirichlet_boundary_convergent (t : ℝ) (ht : t ≠ 0) :
∃ (L : ℂ), Tendsto
(fun N => ∑ d ∈ Icc 1 N,
↑(moebius d) * (↑(d : ℕ) : ℂ) ^ (-(1 + 2 * ↑t * I)))
atTop (nhds L) := by
sorry
